summary: Buildable as written on master (a81d19c) with three small implementation fixes, and a useful control for the parent. Two expectations are wrong: on master the w2 zero-store is already OFF, and removing -1 tiles saves almost nothing under a non-persistent grid. Read it as master's scalar-dequant Triton engine vs Marlin at turn_4, with first_turn expected flat, not faster.
justification: SGLang's moe_align_block_size places -1 routes in an extra padded bucket (num_experts+1, ids shifted +1, expert_ids -1); master's '33*(BLOCK_T-1)' capacity comment and _check_expert_gemms' -1 block agree. But _nvfp4_moe_gemm sizes its grid from the static capacity (221 vs 220 token tiles at turn_4) and the kernel early-exits both -1 tiles and past-n_padded tiles, so removing -1 tiles only swaps one early-exit for another; only the parent's n_padded-bounded persistent loop cashes it in. zero_nonlocal_w2 is already OFF on master (every log prints '[w2 zero-store] OFF'). At turn_4 the Marlin path already uses _align_parallel. What remains is Triton (scalar dequant, BLOCK_T 128/BLOCK_W 128/8w/3s) vs Marlin at turn_4: stages 2/3 ran 2100-2318 us vs Marlin 2115-2217; flat expected; ~7% row drift. Weakest link: first_turn 'faster 1-3%': part (3) at T=16384 was measured twice (align-local-parallel-first-turn 0.977-0.990; stack-tonight-six-prefill 0.980-1.007); expect flat to ~-1%. turn_1 stays on Marlin, a clean drift control.
confounders: experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn (landed): part (1) reverses its turn_4 half; the point of the control; compare to Marlin rows 2148/2115 us.
w2-nonlocal-zero-store-off-first-turn (landed): zero-store already off; zero_nonlocal=False changes nothing; do not credit it.

stack-tonight-five-prefill / moe-align-local-routes-parallel-port: if the extended self-check is folded into align_par_ok, a failure also turns off Marlin's parallel align and confounds; use a separate flag.
moe-align-32-experts-first-turn: one token tile of grid difference, negligible.
interference: No companion. Parent turn_4 minus control turn_4 = persistent-grid effect plus the -1-tile removal only a persistent grid can cash in. Implementation fixes: (a) separate flag state['align_par_triton_ok'] for the Triton-path align self-check, leaving align_par_ok untouched; (b) _experts reads state.get('marlin_max_tokens', MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS) instead of the module global (or the fallback writes it with global); (c) warm _align_parallel for BSM 128 and 256 in prepare() before capture. The NaN-poison check largely duplicates _weighted_sum_skips_remote; gating on state['zero_nonlocal_w2'] being False is sufficient. _check_experts_e2e needs a token-count argument for T=3012.
rules_flags: None blocking: gate on x.shape[0] only; align/n_padded/grid on device; checks and fallback decided in untimed prepare() on synthetic data; NVFP4 unchanged.
open_questions: Optionally print n_padded at T=3012 in prepare() with both aligns to confirm ~165 tiles difference.
If the control loses at turn_4 by more than ~7%, the parent must win by more than that margin before the gate move is worth keeping.
